Symbol Dictionary

¶9. The Church in the Wilderness — the Mountains Keep the Faith

Section 9 of 12 · ≈18 min

In This Section

The two classes cross into the Christian era unchanged: when the church married the empire, the true church — the woman of Revelation 12 — fled into the wilderness, and for 1260 prophetic days the mountains kept the faith that the mingled majority in the plains and cities had surrendered.

Scripture likens God's people to a woman — the true church defined — Jer. 6:2; Rev. 12:1-2; Eph. 5:25, 27:

  • Jer. 6:2. "I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate [woman]" — Scripture's own key, laid down before the symbol is used: God Himself likens His covenant people, the daughter of Zion, to a woman. The Bible defines its own figure.
  • Rev. 12:1. "And there appeared a great wonder in heaven; a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars" — the woman appears: arrayed in Christ's righteousness, standing on the covenant, crowned with the twelve. She is a corporate body of the faithful, not a city and not a numbers-majority.
    • the woman = the true church, the seed of the woman corporate — the pure bride of Christ, kept distinct by loyalty, not by numbers; God's own likeness for the daughter of Zion (Jer. 6:2; Rev. 12:1-2; Eph. 5:25, 27; Rev. 12:17).
  • Rev. 12:2. "And she being with child cried, travailing in birth, and pained to be delivered" — the true church bears Christ into the world through suffering; her identity is a birthing loyalty, not comfort or crowds. She is the woman of the enmity — the seed-bearing line of Genesis 3:15 traced from "The Enmity — Two Seeds from One Fall."
  • Eph. 5:25. "Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it" — the church is Christ's bride, the pure woman; this is why Scripture figures apostasy as adultery — the woman who marries another has forsaken her true Husband.
  • Eph. 5:27. "That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish" — the true woman is defined by purity kept, not popularity gained: "not having spot" — the exact opposite of the mingled majority.

Two women, two classes — the bride and the harlot — Rev. 17:5; James 4:4; COL 283.3:

  • Rev. 17:5. "And upon her forehead [was] a name written, MYSTERY, BABYLON THE GREAT, THE MOTHER OF HARLOTS AND ABOMINATIONS OF THE EARTH" — the counter-woman. Prophecy sets two women over against each other: the faithful bride, and the harlot who DID marry the world — Babylon, the city-system of "Babel — Congregating for Convenience" wearing a woman's name. Two women, two classes; there is no third.
  • James 4:4. "Ye adulterers and adulteresses, know ye not that the friendship of the world is enmity with God? whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God" — the great mingling named in one line: a church seeking the friendship of the world commits spiritual adultery. This is the exact mechanism of the fourth-century union.
  • WitnessCOL 283.3. White: "There are only two classes in the world today, and only two classes will be recognized in the judgment—those who violate God's law and those who obey it. Christ gives the test by which to prove our loyalty or disloyalty" — the two-classes doctrine in bare form: the line runs on obedience to God's commandments, exactly the mark of the woman's remnant seed (Rev. 12:17).

The great mingling repeats — the church marries the empire — GC 43.1; GC 45.1; PP 81.2:

  • WitnessGC 43.1. White: "Most of the Christians at last consented to lower their standard, and a union was formed between Christianity and paganism... the Christian religion became corrupted, and the church lost her purity and power. There were some, however, who were not misled by these delusions" — the historical fact: under Constantine the "converted" pagan masses brought their customs in, and the church that stopped fleeing the world lost her purity — while a faithful few refused, splitting the two classes again.
  • WitnessGC 45.1. White: "But there is no union between the Prince of light and the prince of darkness, and there can be no union between their followers... He then brought his power to bear more fully upon these, and inspired them to persecute those who remained true to God" — the union of convenience turns persecuting: Satan, having led the compromised church further from truth, "inspired them to persecute those who remained true to God." This is precisely what drives the woman to flee.
  • WitnessPP 81.2. White: "For some time the two classes remained separate. The race of Cain... dispersed over the plains and valleys where the children of Seth had dwelt; and the latter, in order to escape from their contaminating influence, withdrew to the mountains... So long as this separation continued, they maintained the worship of God in its purity. But in the lapse of time they ventured, little by little, to mingle with the inhabitants of the valleys" — the master pattern from before the flood (see “The Mingling — How the Peculiar People Lost Their Peculiarity”): Cain's race in the plains, the faithful in the mountains, worship kept pure only while separate. The Christian era now repeats it point for point.

The woman flees — the wilderness and the 1260 days — Rev. 12:6, 14; MWM 213.1:

  • Rev. 12:6. "And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God, that they should feed her there a thousand two hundred [and] threescore days" — the section's title text. When the empire married the church, the true church did not conquer the plains — she FLED, kept distinct by separation, fed by God in a place He prepared, for the 1260 prophetic days.
    • the wilderness = the place of preservation-by-separation for the true church during the mingled centuries — not a geography but a condition: God's provided refuge, entered by flight rather than conquest, where the woman is fed away from the serpent through the 1260 days/years (Rev. 12:6; Rev. 12:14; Heb. 11:38; 2 Cor. 6:17).
  • Rev. 12:14. "And to the woman were given two wings of a great eagle, that she might fly into the wilderness, into her place, where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time, from the face of the serpent" — the flight restated: God's own provision (eagle's wings, cf. Ex. 19:4) carries the church into HER place, nourished away from the serpent for time + times + half a time — the same 1260, the medieval night.
  • WitnessMWM 213.1. Miller: "Three times we have witnessed... the fulfilment of the 'time, times, and an half,' in the accomplishment of the 'forty-two months,' in the completion of the 'twelve hundred and three-score days'" — the pioneer reading: time, times, and a half = forty-two months = 1260 days, one period, its fulfilment already witnessed.

The mountains keep the faith — Heb. 11:37-38; GC 64.1; 65.2-3; 267.2:

  • Heb. 11:37. "They were stoned, they were sawn asunder, were tempted, were slain with the sword: they wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins; being destitute, afflicted, tormented" — the roll of the faithful reaches the persecuted witnesses: the same class as the wilderness woman, marked by loss for the truth's sake.
  • Heb. 11:38. "(Of whom the world was not worthy:) they wandered in deserts, and [in] mountains, and [in] dens and caves of the earth" — the faith chapter's roll of the persecuted ends here: "in deserts, and in mountains." And the verdict is inverted from all appearance — the mingled majority that held the cities and called itself the church was the world "not worthy" of the exiles it hunted. The mountain-and-plain geography of the two classes holds (see “The Two Lineages — the City and the Name”).
  • WitnessGC 64.1. White: "There were some, however, who refused to yield to the authority of pope or prelate... A separation took place. Those who adhered to the ancient faith now withdrew... others retreated to the secluded glens and rocky fastnesses of the mountains, and there preserved their freedom to worship God" — PP 81 replayed point for point: "A separation took place," and the faithful "retreated... to the mountains" — the Waldenses, the wilderness woman in the flesh.
  • WitnessGC 65.2. White: "They declared the Church of Rome to be the apostate Babylon of the Apocalypse... Through ages of darkness and apostasy there were Waldenses who denied the supremacy of Rome, who rejected image worship as idolatry, and who kept the true Sabbath" — the mountain church stands opposite the counter-woman of Rev. 17:5: they named Rome the apostate Babylon, and their mark was obedience — the true Sabbath kept — the same commandment-line that runs to "The Seal or the Mark — the Distinction Made Visible."
  • WitnessGC 65.3. White: "Behind the lofty bulwarks of the mountains—in all ages the refuge of the persecuted and oppressed—the Waldenses found a hiding place. Here the light of truth was kept burning amid the darkness of the Middle Ages. Here, for a thousand years, witnesses for the truth maintained the ancient faith" — the mountains as the wilderness refuge, truth "kept burning" through the medieval night. (The "thousand years" is the round historical span of the Middle Ages; the precise prophetic measure is the 1260 of Rev. 12:6, 14.)
  • WitnessGC 267.2. White: "God's witnesses remained in a state of obscurity... hunted, betrayed, tortured, buried in dungeon cells, martyred for their faith, or compelled to flee to mountain fastnesses, and to dens and caves of the earth—then the faithful witnesses prophesied in sackcloth. Yet they continued their testimony throughout the entire period of 1260 years" — the direct bridge from text to history: the witnesses driven to "dens and caves of the earth" (Heb. 11:38 verbatim) through the 1260 years — the wilderness woman and the sackcloth witnesses are one company.

No cathedral — worship in spirit and in truth — John 4:21, 23-24; GC 66.1-2:

  • John 4:21. "Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father" — Christ DE-localizes worship: it is bound to no city, no temple, no shrine. The point is not that mountains are the appointed place of worship — it is that worship is freed from place entirely, so the wilderness church needs no cathedral.
  • John 4:23. "But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him" — the true worshippers carry a portable altar — the pilgrim worship of Abraham's tent-altars in "Abraham and Lot — the Tent and the Plain" — and this is exactly how the woman worships in the wilderness: no building, full acceptance with God.
  • John 4:24. "God [is] a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship [him] in spirit and in truth" — the definition of acceptable worship is inward loyalty, not architecture: the ground for reading the wilderness centuries as genuine, God-accepted worship.
  • WitnessGC 66.1. White: "God had provided for His people a sanctuary of awful grandeur, befitting the mighty truths committed to their trust. To those faithful exiles the mountains were an emblem of the immutable righteousness of Jehovah... God's servants should be as firm as the unchanging hills" — no cathedral, and none needed: God's own provision was their sanctuary, and the mountains preached His law's immutability to those who kept it.
  • WitnessGC 66.2. White: "They thanked God that He had provided for them an asylum from the wrath and cruelty of men. They rejoiced in their freedom to worship before Him... From many a lofty cliff they chanted the praise of God, and the armies of Rome could not silence their songs of thanksgiving" — the "place prepared of God" of Rev. 12:6 realized: an asylum from the dragon's wrath where the woman worships freely, in spirit and in truth.

Separation is the standing command — the line runs to the remnant — 2 Cor. 6:17-18; Rev. 12:17; 18:4; MWM 316.2:

  • 2 Cor. 6:17. "Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean [thing]; and I will receive you" — the command that defines the class in every age: SEPARATION. The wilderness flight is this imperative obeyed under persecution.
  • 2 Cor. 6:18. "And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty" — the reward of separation is sonship: the place "prepared of God" is where He receives and fathers those who came out.
  • WitnessMWM 316.2. Miller: "A church, according to the Scriptures, is a religious assembly, selected and called out of the world, by the doctrine of the gospel, to worship the true God according to his word... we have... 'the church in the wilderness,' Acts 7:38" — the pioneer definition: the church is by nature CALLED OUT of the world; "the church in the wilderness" is one of Scripture's own names for her.
  • Rev. 12:17. "And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ" — the wilderness woman is one continuous line ending in a commandment-keeping remnant. The mark of the true class is never numbers but obedience and testimony — the seed of the woman of "The Enmity — Two Seeds from One Fall," carried forward to "The Seal or the Mark — the Distinction Made Visible."
  • Rev. 18:4. "And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues" — the same come-out call re-sounded at the end. The wilderness principle is not medieval-only: it is the standing summons out of the church-world union, from Constantine's day to the final call of "Come Out, My People — the Pilgrim Call."

Synthesis

DEFINITION — THE CHURCH IN THE WILDERNESS — THE MOUNTAINS KEEP THE FAITH = the two classes cross into the Christian era unchanged. The true church is the woman — Scripture's own likeness for the daughter of Zion (Jer. 6:2), the pure bride Christ loved and will present "not having spot" (Eph. 5:25, 27), clothed with the sun and travailing to bear Christ to the world (Rev. 12:1-2) — and her counterfeit is the harlot Babylon who married the world (Rev. 17:5), for "the friendship of the world is enmity with God" (James 4:4). When the fourth-century church consented to a "union... between Christianity and paganism" and "lost her purity and power" (GC 43.1), the mingling of Genesis 6 repeated inside the church, and Satan inspired the compromised body to persecute those who remained true to God (GC 45.1); so the woman FLED into the wilderness, to "a place prepared of God," fed and nourished on eagle's wings away from the serpent for the 1260 days — a time, times, and half a time, the forty-two months, one period (Rev. 12:6, 14; MWM 213.1). The wilderness is a condition, not a shrine: Hebrews locates the faithful "in deserts, and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth," a class "of whom the world was not worthy" (Heb. 11:37-38), and history fills in the names — the pattern of PP 81 replayed point for point: "a separation took place," and the faithful "retreated... to the mountains" (GC 64.1; PP 81.2) — the Waldenses, who named Rome the apostate Babylon and kept the true Sabbath (GC 65.2), keeping the light burning "behind the lofty bulwarks of the mountains" through the medieval night (GC 65.3), the very words in which the 1260-year witnesses prophesied in sackcloth (GC 267.2). Their worship needed no cathedral, for Christ had freed worship from every place — "neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem," but "in spirit and in truth" (John 4:21-24) — and God Himself provided their sanctuary and asylum (GC 66.1-2). The abiding law of the class is "come out from among them, and be ye separate" answered by sonship (2 Cor. 6:17-18; MWM 316.2), and the wilderness line ends in a remnant "which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ" (Rev. 12:17; COL 283.3) — the same summons still sounding at the end: "Come out of her, my people" (Rev. 18:4). The mingled majority held the cities and the name, and called itself the church; the mountains kept the faith.

Symbols Defined Here

  • the woman = the true church, the seed of the woman corporate — the pure bride of Christ, kept distinct by loyalty rather than numbers; God likens the daughter of Zion to a woman, Christ loves the church as a husband his wife "not having spot," and her remnant seed keep the commandments of God and the testimony of Jesus, over against the harlot Babylon who married the world (Jer. 6:2; Rev. 12:1-2, 17; Eph. 5:25, 27; Rev. 17:5).
  • the wilderness = the place of preservation-by-separation for the true church during the mingled centuries — a condition, not a geography: God's provided refuge, entered by flight and not conquest, where the woman is fed away from the serpent through the 1260 days/years; needing no cathedral because worship is "in spirit and in truth," and located by Scripture itself "in deserts, and in mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth" (Rev. 12:6, 14; Heb. 11:38; John 4:23-24; 2 Cor. 6:17).

Symbols Carried

the enmity and the two seeds, the God-put division this section traces through the Christian era (see “The Enmity — Two Seeds from One Fall”); mountains and plains, the geography of the two classes that the Waldenses repeat point for point (see “The Two Lineages — the City and the Name”); the mingling, the church-marries-empire mechanism of the fourth-century fall (see “The Mingling — How the Peculiar People Lost Their Peculiarity”); Babel / Babylon, the city-system the harlot of Rev. 17:5 names on her forehead (see “Babel — Congregating for Convenience”); the tent and the altar and pilgrims and strangers, the portable in-spirit-and-truth worship the mountain church inherited (see “Abraham and Lot — the Tent and the Plain”); the peculiar people and dwelling alone, the covenant identity the wilderness preserved (see "Israel Mingles — "Like All the Nations""); the commandments-and-faith remnant of Rev. 12:17, drawn out to its final visible form (see “The Seal or the Mark — the Distinction Made Visible”); the come-out call of Rev. 18:4, sounded in full at the close (see “Come Out, My People — the Pilgrim Call”).

For Discussion

  1. The woman's mark is never numbers: she flees while the majority holds the cities and the name, and Scripture says the world "was not worthy" of the wanderers in the mountains (Rev. 12:6; Heb. 11:38). Where do we still measure the true church — or our own standing — by size, visibility, or institutional standing, and what would it change to measure by Rev. 12:17's two marks, the commandments of God and the testimony of Jesus?
  2. The church fell not by persecution but by friendship: "a union was formed between Christianity and paganism" when the standard was lowered (GC 43.1), and "the friendship of the world is enmity with God" (James 4:4). What "half-converted" customs and alliances press on the church now, and how do we refuse the union without refusing the people?
  3. Christ freed worship from every place: "neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem... in spirit and in truth" (John 4:21, 23) — so the Waldenses worshiped fully accepted with no cathedral (GC 66.1-2). What would it change this week if your acceptance with God rested wholly on inward loyalty rather than on place, building, or crowd — and what "portable altar" would that require you to carry?
